title: Console triage heuristics + sprint 22 scope notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc to align console UX + tooling backlog triage rules ahead of Sprint 22 planning (release window: 2026-07-20 -> 2026-08-02). The goal: produce a small, high-confidence cut list that protects our customer-facing rollout milestones while keeping low-risk polish and experiments deferred.

Context and constraints:
- Recent incidents (CON-4123) surfaced masking/visibility gaps in route-level tracing; infra has a partial fix but console surface needs a short-term UX mitigation (reduces support noise).
- Product commitment to rollout per-route rollout controls in v2 by end of July (epic CON-4187) — visible in dashboards and rollout policy editor.
- Team capacity: 3 FE engineers (2 mid+1 junior), 2 PMs, 1 UX, 1 QA for the sprint. Infra/BE availability limited (on-call rotation).

Stakeholders:
- Priya Nair (owner, product)
- Marcos Rivera (eng lead, console)
- Evelyn Zhou (UX)
- SRE: Ben Gallagher (support for tracing work)
- Solutions engineering (feedback loop for rollout UI)

Triage heuristics (high-level):
We need repeatable heuristics to score backlog items. Use this ordering to recommend sprint inclusions. Items are bucketed by Priority: P0, P1, P2, P3.

P0 (must ship this sprint):
- Blocks rollout or causes customer-visible data loss/regression.
- Security/compliance items with active customer impact (e.g., audit log missing fields).
- Anything landing in the GA rollout path we promised (CON-4187 MVP gates).

P1 (strongly prefer this sprint):
- High ROI for support reduction (>=20% ticket volume reduction estimate) or removes major confusion in onboarding flows.
- Low-to-medium engineering effort (<=3 dev-weeks) and low BE coupling.

P2 (nice-to-have):
- UX polish, wireframe iterations, or features that are behind feature flags.
- Medium effort and medium dependencies. Defer if P0/P1 scope grows.

P3 (backlog / discovery):
- Research spikes, big refactors, or long-running experiments.
- Move to product roadmap grooming later.

Scoring model (quick numeric to prioritize):
Score = Impact*2 + EffortScore*(-1) + RiskPenalty*(-1) + CustomerEscalation*2
Where:
- Impact: 1 low / 2 medium / 3 high
- EffortScore: 1 small / 2 medium / 3 large (we subtract this)
- RiskPenalty: 1 low / 2 med / 3 high (unknown infra coupling increases this)
- CustomerEscalation: 0 none / 1 some / 2 active
Pick items with highest Score; tie-breaker = customer escalations then time-sensitivity.

Wireframe / UX quick notes (for Evelyn to iterate):
1) Rollout policy editor: add an inline 'preview' toggler that shows which routes will be affected when a policy is saved. (Sketch: left pane policy rules, right pane live-route list with simple badges). Reason: reduces accidental broad rollouts.
Acceptance criteria: toggler present, preview lists up to 50 routes, page loads < 800ms for heavy projects.

2) Route-level tracing CTA: small banner on route detail if trace coverage < 80% with link to 'enable tracing' flow. (banner copy: "Tracing incomplete — enable to see per-token latency breakdowns").
Acceptance criteria: banner appears only when infra flag is on; clicking opens modal with single CTA.

3) Model variant fallback UX: inside inference config, expose a compact heuristic summary: "Preferred: redwood/v1.13 • Fallbacks: redwood/ql-8q". Clicking expands differences.
Acceptance: text shorthand + expand/collapse; link to docs.

Sprint 22 candidate backlog items (raw groomed list + suggested bucket):
- CON-4239: Route tracing banner + quick-enable modal — P0 (owner: Marcos)
  Rationale: tied to active support tickets; low BE work (feature flag + modal).
- CON-4187-1: Policy preview UI (mvp) — P0 (owner: Evelyn + Marcos)
  Rationale: GA commitment; score high on customer confidence; moderate FE work but BE endpoints exist.
- CON-4301: Console keyboard shortcuts (nav) — P2 (owner: Anika)
  Rationale: polish; deferrable.
- CON-4277: Rollout history export (CSV) — P1 (owner: Liam)
  Rationale: required by one enterprise pilot; small BE pagination work.
- CON-4310: Wireframe: compact alert inbox (visual polish) — P3 (owner: Evelyn)
  Rationale: lower priority.
- CON-4290: Hotfix: telemetry sanitizer for secrets in logs — P0 (owner: Ben)
  Rationale: compliance risk, must ship.

Proposed cut list for Sprint 22 (reduce scope to fit team):
Inclusions (commit):
- CON-4239 (tracing banner + modal) — quick win, high support ROI.
- CON-4187-1 (policy preview MVP) — core GA commitment.
- CON-4290 (telemetry sanitizer) — compliance/security.

Drop / Defer to Sprint 23: 
- CON-4301 (keyboard shortcuts)
- CON-4310 (alert inbox wireframe)
- Larger deeply-coupled features: CON-4123 full tracing refactor (infra-led) — leave as BE workqueue.

Scope assumptions and risk log:
- Assumes BE will expose route-preview API with pagination (EPIC owner: infra). If BE cannot deliver by 2026-07-15, move policy preview to feature-flagged alpha (soft launch) or cut.
- Risk: junior FE bandwidth — plan two 1:1 pairing days with Marcos to unblock critical pieces.

Testing and QA notes:
- QA will focus on critical flows: policy save/preview, enable tracing modal path, and telemetry scrubber. Test matrix enumerated in linked Jira subtasks.
- Performance targets: page load goals noted in acceptance criteria above.

Rollout and rollout safety: 
- All features go behind console-feature flags; enable for pilots first. Use canary rollout: 10% internal -> 25% pilot accounts -> full. Monitor error budget and support tickets for 72 hours after enable.

Open questions (for sprint kickoff):
1) What is the maximum acceptable response time for the route-preview endpoint under heavy projects? (ask infra)
2) Should policy preview include deprecated routes or filter them out? Option: opt-out excluded by default. (product decision)
3) Who will sign off on copy for tracing banner? (suggest: Evelyn + support lead)

Decisions logged (so far):
- Tracing banner modal is in-scope and counts as P0 mitigation (decision by Priya 2026-07-04).
- Policy preview MVP will show up to 50 routes and will be paginated (agreed 2026-07-06).

Next steps (owner -> action -> due):
- Marcos -> break down CON-4239 into 3 dev subtasks -> 2026-07-09
- Evelyn -> produce 2 wireframe variants for policy preview + banner modal -> 2026-07-08
- Ben -> produce telemetry scrub checklist & small BE task list -> 2026-07-09
- Priya -> finalize sprint cut list and post to Jira sprint planning board -> 2026-07-12

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally mixes rough heuristics and concrete acceptance criteria. During sprint planning we'll convert each committed item into 1-3 actionable Jira subtasks with owners and estimates. If you see a scope item that looks large, flag it now — prefer to split or defer.

- CON-4187 (policy rollout epic) -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CON-4187
